prompt: Write a short blog post about the weather and how it has changed your plans. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the post only.
final_message:
# The Rain Had Other Ideas

I had a plan for this week, and it was a good one. On Saturday I meant to drive out to the lake, spread a blanket under the big maple, and eat a sandwich while the leaves did their showing off. I had even bought the good bread.

The weather had other ideas. It started raining Thursday night, and by Friday morning the sky looked like a wet wool blanket hung over the whole county. The forecast promised more of the same through Sunday, which I took personally.

I will admit I sulked for about an hour. I stood at the kitchen window with my tea and told the clouds what I thought of them, and they did not answer. Then the tea went cold, and I figured I could either keep complaining or find something useful to do with a wet Saturday.

So the lake trip became a kitchen day. I pulled out the flour and the last of the apples from the bag a neighbor left on my porch, and I made a pie. It was not the pie I had planned, because I had meant to buy the nice cinnamon, and the old jar in my cupboard has seen better years. It tasted fine anyway, and the house smelled like a bakery by noon.

The rest of the day went better than I deserved. I finally sorted the drawer of old letters I have been putting off since spring, and I found one from a friend that made me laugh out loud, alone in my living room, like a person who has lost her mind. I wrote her back that same afternoon. The mail won't carry it until Monday, but it is written, and that counts for something.

By evening the rain had settled into a steady patter on the roof, the kind you can hear from every room. I sat with a slice of pie and a blanket, and I will tell you plainly that I did not miss the lake one bit. The picnic will keep. The maple will still be there next weekend, though maybe with fewer leaves, and I can live with that.

What I keep coming back to is how easily a changed plan can turn into a better day, if you let it. I do not always manage that. This time I did, and I am pleased with myself.

If your weekend got rained out too, I hope you found a pie of your own to make. And if you have good cinnamon, send some my way.

Hattie
